title: Netflix issues its biggest layoff in four years
key_facts: Netflix is eliminating roughly 1,000 jobs, about 6% of its workforce, in a restructuring announced Wednesday (14 Oct 2026).
Cuts fall largely on product, technology, legal and human resources teams.
Netflix had about 16,000 full-time employees at the end of 2025; revenue reached almost $25 billion in the first half of 2026, up 15%.
Stock is down 22% this year and 42% over 12 months; Netflix lost a bidding war for Warner Bros. Discovery in February.
Co-CEOs Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters said the business is strong and on track for its full-year forecast.
Earlier cuts in May and June 2022 were about 150 and 300 jobs.
quote_evidence: The company is eliminating roughly 1,000 jobs, about 6% of its workforce, in a restructuring announced Wednesday.
The cuts fall largely on its product, technology, legal, and human resources teams.
Netflix has plenty of money, but a growth problem.
why_it_matters_hint: Large cut at a streaming giant; Fortune ties it to slower growth, not to AI.
notes: Fortune does not link the layoff to AI. Pool score 7 lowered to 6 because the AI angle is absent from the article.
